subject: typescript
title: Type narrowing
description: typeof and in guards, discriminated unions, truthiness narrowing and exhaustive switches.

content.title: Definition
content.body: Narrowing is how TypeScript follows your control flow. Inside a branch where a check has passed, the union shrinks to the constituents that could still be there, and the members of those become available.

content.title: Discriminated union
content.body: Give every member a literal tag and a switch does the narrowing for you — this is the pattern behind the app's own Exercise type.

content.title: Good practice
content.body: Add a default branch that assigns the value to never. When a new union member appears, that line fails to compile and points you at every place that has to handle it.

exercises.question: TypeScript · narrowing
exercises.back: Narrows x to string inside the branch
exercises.explanation: A typeof guard narrows a union so string-only members become available.

exercises.question: What is the type of x on the marked line?
exercises.explanation: Inside the guard only the number constituent remains, which is why toFixed is available. After the if, x is string.

exercises.question: What does assigning the switch value to a never-typed variable in the default branch achieve?

answers.text: It throws a helpful runtime error
It turns a newly added union member into a compile error at every unhandled switch

exercises.explanation: If every member is handled, the value is narrowed to never and the assignment is fine. Add a member and the assignment stops compiling.

exercises.question: Complete the guard that distinguishes the two shapes by property presence.
exercises.explanation: The in operator narrows a union to the members that declare that property. hasOwnProperty does not narrow.

exercises.question: Which line hides a bug when count is 0?

answers.text: Line 2 — 0 is falsy, so a real count of zero reports "unknown"
Line 1 — an optional number parameter is not allowed
Line 5 — the return types must match

exercises.explanation: Truthiness narrowing removes 0 along with undefined. Test count !== undefined when zero is a legitimate value.

exercises.question: A function returning `x is Cat` lets the compiler narrow at the call site.
exercises.explanation: That is a user-defined type guard. The compiler trusts the predicate, so the body has to actually check what it claims.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: A discriminated union needs every member to share a ___ property with a literal type.
exercises.explanation: The discriminant is one property present in every member, whose literal type differs between them — kind, type, status.

exercises.question: Why does the compiler complain on the marked line?

answers.text: Narrowing never applies inside arrow functions
x must be annotated again inside the callback
setTimeout callbacks cannot read outer variables
It does not for a parameter — but narrowing is discarded for a mutable variable captured in a closure

exercises.explanation: Control-flow analysis cannot know when a deferred callback runs, so narrowing on anything reassignable is dropped. Copy it into a const first.

exercises.question: Which check narrows `string | string[]` to the array branch?
exercises.explanation: Array.isArray is typed as a type guard. typeof never returns "array", and length exists on both constituents so it narrows nothing.

exercises.question: Why does this guard fail to exclude null?

answers.text: typeof null is 'object', so null is still in the narrowed type
typeof does not work on object types

exercises.explanation: A JavaScript wart the type system faithfully models. Test `if (x)` or `x !== null` instead.

exercises.question: What does a function declared `asserts value is string` do?

answers.text: Narrows the argument for the rest of the scope, on the promise that it throws otherwise
Returns a boolean the caller must check
Adds a runtime type check automatically
Casts the value without any effect

exercises.explanation: Unlike a predicate it returns nothing: control flow after the call implies the assertion held. It must be called on a variable with an explicit type annotation to work.

exercises.question: Complete the guard that narrows an unknown error to Error.
exercises.explanation: catch binds unknown under useUnknownInCatchVariables, so this guard is what makes .message available. Errors crossing a realm boundary can defeat instanceof.

exercises.question: Narrowing obj.value with a typeof check survives an intervening function call.
exercises.explanation: Any call could reassign the property, so control-flow analysis discards the narrowing. Copy it into a const first.

exercises.question: Why is items still (string | null)[] on line 2?
exercises.code:
1  const raw: (string | null)[] = ['a', null];
2  const items = raw.filter((x) => x !== null);

answers.text: filter is typed to return the same element type unless the callback is a type predicate
filter does not accept arrow functions

exercises.explanation: Write `(x): x is string => x !== null` — or, from TypeScript 5.5, the inference does it for you when the callback is a simple predicate.

exercises.question: Given `a: string | number` and `b: string | boolean`, what is a's type inside `if (a === b)`?

answers.text: string — the only type both unions share

exercises.explanation: Equality narrows both operands to their common members, because only those can compare equal under strict equality.
